thread:
maria: Quick q — the compliance audit asked us to shorten retention for 'low-sensitivity' app logs to 90 days. Before I flip the SIEM export, any red flags for incident/vuln triage or forensics?
alex: Short answer: depends. Which streams are you classifying as low-sensitivity? auth/audit vs app-debug vs metrics?
devon: Proposed groups matter. If it's pure debug + feature flags, 90d is usually ok. But request traces can be borderline if they contain PII.
maria: Proposed mapping: app-debug, feature-flags, and non-auth request traces => 90d. auth events, infra/syslog, security alerts => 365d.
samir: If we drop debug to 90d we need a JIT path for old traces during investigations. Also think through KMS unwrap flow for archives — who can unseal?
maria: Good call. My plan was: export to SIEM for 90d, after that lifecycle job moves to cold S3 bucket encrypted with KMS alias/reds-sei-logs. Access only via ticket+JIT role. Thoughts?
alex: Sounds reasonable. Concretely: 1) lifecycle rule to move after 90d 2) archive bucket encrypted with dedicated KMS key 3) a JIT role (forensics:temp-unwrap) that can be assumed for n hours after approval 4) unwrap operations recorded in audit logs.
devon: Sample retention + IAM snippets:```yaml
# retention-lifecycle.yml
rules:
  - id: move-to-cold
    prefix: "app-debug/"
    status: Enabled
    transition:
      - days: 90
        storage_class: GLACIER
  - id: expire-debug
    prefix: "app-debug/"
    status: Enabled
    expiration:
      days: 365
```
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:DescribeKey"],"Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx","Condition":{"Bool":{"aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent":"true"}}}
  ]
}
```
ops-bot: retention-job-prod scheduled nightly for archive-job-prod (run ID 2026-04-02T03:00Z).
tay: One other risk: several partners pull SIEM exports for analytics. If we shorten retention we must notify them and provide a migration/export window or they will miss data.
samir: From vuln-triage POV: sometimes we need stack traces >90d for root cause. Proposal: for high-sev incidents create an encrypted evidence escrow snapshot kept 1yr, keyed to incident ticket and accessible via JIT unseal. That avoids keeping all debug logs hot.
maria: That balances cost and forensics. Can we define the JIT process? Ticket + two approvers + automatic audit trail?
alex: Yes. Minimal flow: 1) open ticket SEC-XXXX 2) pager oncall + eng-lead approve in ticket 3) ops run unwrap task that logs KMS decrypt and copies artifacts to ephemeral forensics bucket 4) role revoked after 4 hours. Add automated checks that ensure all accesses are recorded to audit-log.
devon: Also need to update runbooks and test unwrap on a dry-run. Test vectors: UUIDs, sample logs, and a replay script to validate we can reconstruct request chains.
maria: I'll draft an RFC and include all this. Action items I see: update retention yaml, create JIT IAM role + runbook, KMS rotation/owner assigned, partner notification plan, cost estimate, and forensic dry-run.
alex: + add monitoring alert if archive-job fails for >1 day and a regression check that we can restore sample object within 1 hour.
maria: I'll open RFC/ticket now: https://redwood.internal/r/SEC-5234 (placeholder). Will @ops oncall once draft is ready. Thanks everyone :pray:
samir: :thumbsup: also +1 for adding a brief SLA in RFC for forensic restores so incident managers know expectations.
tay: tagging integrations team in RFC so they can respond to partner impact.
maria: great — I'll include owners and estimated timelines in the RFC. If anyone wants to add sample IAM statements or playbook text paste here and I'll include it.
